title: Inflation expectations (UMich)
description: University of Michigan Surveys of Consumers. A SEPARATE board from Positioning on purpose: it shares no market, no cadence and no denominator with the CFTC data, and putting a monthly survey on the same canvas as weekly futures positioning invites reading a relationship that nothing here tests. Percentile ranks are causal, precomputed in pandas by scripts/build, and each is taken over its own declared regime pool -- see lib/umich_spec.

panels.title: Expected price change, next year and next 5-10 years (median, % per year)
panels.description: MEDIAN, not mean -- the mean is dragged by a fat right tail and is a different number. And the question asks about 'prices in general', not the CPI: it is a household expectation, not a forecast of a published index. Both series are in % per year, which is why they share one axis. The 1-year series is only continuous from 1982-03 and the 5-10 year series from 1990-04; before those dates the question was worded differently or asked sporadically, so the line has real holes and they are drawn as holes.

targets.rawQueryText: SELECT ts/1000 AS time, infl_exp_1y AS 'next 1 year', infl_exp_5y10y AS 'next 5-10 years' FROM board_inflation WHERE ts BETWEEN $__from AND $__to ORDER BY ts
targets.queryText: SELECT ts/1000 AS time, infl_exp_1y AS 'next 1 year', infl_exp_5y10y AS 'next 5-10 years' FROM board_inflation WHERE ts BETWEEN $__from AND $__to ORDER BY ts

panels.title: Where each expectation sits in its own history (causal percentile)
panels.description: Each month ranked only against months up to and including itself, within its own regime pool. A rank is BLANK rather than approximated when its pool is shorter than 36 observations -- the rule lives in the data, not in an if-statement inside this panel.

targets.rawQueryText: SELECT ts/1000 AS time, infl_exp_1y_pctile AS '1 year pctile', infl_exp_5y10y_pctile AS '5-10 year pctile' FROM board_inflation WHERE ts BETWEEN $__from AND $__to ORDER BY ts
targets.queryText: SELECT ts/1000 AS time, infl_exp_1y_pctile AS '1 year pctile', infl_exp_5y10y_pctile AS '5-10 year pctile' FROM board_inflation WHERE ts BETWEEN $__from AND $__to ORDER BY ts

panels.title: Sentiment index, and its two components
panels.description: Index points, 1966=100, so all three belong on one axis. There is a break here that the line does NOT show: UMich moved the survey from telephone to web over April-June 2024 and measured the change at -6.6 index points on sentiment. They smeared the transition deliberately, so the level has no visible step -- which is exactly why the percentile for these three columns is computed only over the web era, and is blank while that era is shorter than 36 months.

targets.rawQueryText: SELECT ts/1000 AS time, sentiment AS 'sentiment', current_conditions AS 'current conditions', expectations AS 'expectations' FROM board_inflation WHERE ts BETWEEN $__from AND $__to ORDER BY ts
targets.queryText: SELECT ts/1000 AS time, sentiment AS 'sentiment', current_conditions AS 'current conditions', expectations AS 'expectations' FROM board_inflation WHERE ts BETWEEN $__from AND $__to ORDER BY ts

panels.title: Latest survey
panels.description: The most recent month, with the size of the pool each percentile was measured against. A blank percentile beside a populated pool count means the pool is under the 36-observation floor -- the web era, today.

targets.rawQueryText: SELECT survey_date AS 'month', infl_exp_1y AS '1y expected %', infl_exp_1y_pctile AS '1y pctile', infl_exp_5y10y AS '5-10y expected %', infl_exp_5y10y_pctile AS '5-10y pctile', sentiment AS 'sentiment', sentiment_pool AS 'months ranked against' FROM board_inflation ORDER BY ts DESC LIMIT 1
targets.queryText: SELECT survey_date AS 'month', infl_exp_1y AS '1y expected %', infl_exp_1y_pctile AS '1y pctile', infl_exp_5y10y AS '5-10y expected %', infl_exp_5y10y_pctile AS '5-10y pctile', sentiment AS 'sentiment', sentiment_pool AS 'months ranked against' FROM board_inflation ORDER BY ts DESC LIMIT 1
